## Read 3, DiT half (the full read, both beds, is below)

- Feedback vs single table: -17.4% [-20.0, -15.1]. Needs ≥ 10% with CI > 0 → **met** on DiT.
- Feedback vs each stateless arm run: sym2 -6.9% [-8.4, -5.3]; unif -5.2% [-6.2, -4.1]; cyc4a -5.8% [-6.7, -4.8]; cyc4b -6.3% [-7.5, -5.2] → **beats every stateless arm run**.
- Stateless arms that clear the ≥ 10% bar on DiT: sym2 -11.3% [-13.5, -9.3], unif -12.9% [-15.5, -10.6], cyc4a -12.4% [-14.9, -10.0], cyc4b -11.9% [-14.5, -9.6]. Best stateless arm: **unif**. Feedback adds -5.2% [-6.2, -4.1] over it. The 'stateless is the construction' clause needs feedback to add < 5%: point estimate ≥ 5% → that clause **does not hold** (the CI's lower bound is below 5%, so this is narrow).
- Arm 4 (4-phase cycling, both orders) was **not run** (budget ceiling), so 'beats arms 2–4' is evaluated on arms 2–3 only.
- **Outcome label for feedback:** cancellation **constructed and survived downstream**. The rounding part is bounded at the sites (identity closes to ≤ 1e-7; ‖s_last‖ ≤ Δ/2, ‖Ση‖ ≈ 0.02, ‖Σd‖ ≤ 0.09 on the checked layers). Prediction C/I falls 0.133 → 0.034, and the endpoint falls -17.4% [-20.0, -15.1]. The cumulative site error that remains is the baseline's own input-clip error Σc (identical in both arms, step-constant, never fed back by design). None of the three failure labels (not constructed / lost to representation / lost downstream) applies.
- The per-step reference is *worse* than the single table on this bed (prediction C/I doubles). B′'s '≥ 50% of the per-step gain' criterion has no gain to recover: reported, not applied.

## Stage 3, PixArt-Σ (W16A8 static single table, 1024², 20 steps, MJHQ-64, batch 1, vs bf16 batch-1 references)

Four arms (user decision): single table, feedback, per-step reference, and the best stateless arm from DiT (uniform dither). ±Δ/4 and both 4-phase orders were **cut on PixArt**.

| --- | ---: | --- | ---: | --- | ---: | --- | ---: |
| single table | 0.1844 | — | 18.11 | — | 0.378 | — | 0.0711 |
| uniform dither | 0.1770 | -4.0% [-8.7, +0.8] | 18.31 | +0.20 [-0.05, +0.46] | 0.369 | -0.0086 [-0.0157, -0.0019] | 0.0674 |
| feedback (guarded) | 0.1599 | -13.3% [-17.9, -8.3] | 18.69 | +0.58 [+0.31, +0.86] | 0.393 | +0.0155 [+0.0072, +0.0233] | 0.0404 |
| per-step tables (reference) | 0.1640 | -11.1% [-16.3, -5.8] | 18.58 | +0.47 [+0.20, +0.74] | 0.334 | -0.0442 [-0.0521, -0.0357] | 0.0777 |

- **Feedback vs uniform dither:** latent -9.7% [-13.1, -5.9], ΔPSNR +0.38 dB [+0.17, +0.56], ΔLPIPS +0.0241 [+0.0176, +0.0312].
- **B′ recovery** (the per-step reference gains on PixArt): feedback recovers 120% of its latent gain (criterion ≥ 50%: met).
- **LPIPS gets worse with feedback,** while latent MSE and PSNR improve. Feedback raises per-step prediction-error energy 1.73× on the design cache. The band shares shift toward high frequencies (band 4: 0.203 → 0.217; band 1: 0.352 → 0.320). This is consistent with, not proof of, LPIPS-VGG penalizing the added high-frequency per-step error that PSNR barely sees. The per-step tables give by far the best LPIPS: they shrink the error and keep it coherent, where feedback cancels the coherent part.

## Read 3, both beds

- DiT: feedback -17.4% [-20.0, -15.1] vs the single table; beats every stateless arm run (4 of 4) → **met**.
- PixArt: feedback -13.3% [-17.9, -8.3] and +0.58 dB vs the single table; beats uniform dither -9.7% [-13.1, -5.9] → **met** (±Δ/4 and 4-phase not run on PixArt, by the pre-agreed cut).
- **Read 3: feedback is the construction**, for the arms run. The stateless clause fails on PixArt (uniform dither does not clear ≥ 10%). Caveats: LPIPS worsens on PixArt; two PixArt stateless arms were not run; FID is single-run.

## Feedback cost: instrumented vs deployed

- **Instrumented implementation:** the feedback arm cost 0.66 A30-h for 512 seeds, against 0.22 h for the single table. The instrumented implementation is approximately 3× slower. It uses per-site Python state and diagnostic operations; runtime without diagnostics remains to be measured. One batch of 32 with the counters off took 73.7 s vs 37.0 s for the baseline, and 16.3 s for unquantized sampling (a single timing, not a benchmark).
- **Deployed cost (full feedback):** one fp16 residual tensor per quantizer site, held across steps. Per site and step: one add before the rounding (u = x + s), one subtract after it (r = ũ − q̂), the guard's clamp and the clip, the residual's read and write, and the precision conversion of the stored state. There is no extra matmul. Memory traffic from the residual reads and writes may remain significant even without Python overhead. Compressed feedback (stage 4) adds projection and reconstruction costs.

| model (resolution, tokens) | quantizer sites | residual state per image (2 CFG rows, fp16) | per CFG row |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| DiT-XL/2 (256², 256 tokens) | 112 | 220 MiB | 110 MiB |
| PixArt-Σ (1024², 4,096 tokens), sites as quantized here | 224 | 5.41 GiB | 2.71 GiB |
| PixArt-Σ, attn1 q/k/v sharing one input residual | 168 | 4.43 GiB | 2.21 GiB |

Memory is the real deployment cost: the state scales with tokens × channels summed over every quantized input. On PixArt-Σ at 1024² it is several GiB per image, which is why stage 4's compressed (k-dimensional spatial) state exists.
